column1: Create Endpoints for Upload, Process, Get Result
column22:
h2. Description

The current backend has a monolithic upload-then-process flow that does everything in a single request. For better reliability and user experience (especially with large legal documents), we need a multi-step async workflow:

1. POST /api/v1/documents/upload — Accept a file upload, validate it, save it, and return a document_id immediately.

2. POST /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/process — Trigger processing (text extraction, entity extraction, summarisation) asynchronously. Return a job_id and initial status.

3. GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/result — Return the processed result once processing is complete. Return 202 Accepted with status if still processing.

The existing DocumentController methods should be refactored to support this split workflow.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

⬜ POST /api/v1/documents/upload accepts a file, validates it, saves it, and returns {"document_id": "<uuid>", "status": "uploaded"} with HTTP 201.

⬜ POST /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/process triggers async processing and returns {"job_id": "<uuid>", "status": "processing"} with HTTP 202.

⬜ GET /api/v1/documents/{document_id}/result returns the full result when done (HTTP 200) or {"status": "processing"} when still in progress (HTTP 202).

⬜ Processing includes: text extraction, entity extraction, and LLM summarisation (reusing existing services).

⬜ File validation from magicNums.py is integrated into the upload step.

⬜ Error responses return appropriate HTTP status codes (400 for bad input, 404 for unknown document_id, 500 for server errors).

  • Handle multipart/form-data for file uploads correctly.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

⬜ File upload size is limited to 50MB with a clear error message when exceeded.

⬜ Only allowed file types (PDF, DOCX, TXT, PNG, JPG) are accepted.

⬜ All responses follow a consistent {"success": bool, "data": ..., "error": str|null} format.

column1: Create Comparison Report — Firebase vs Supabase & RDB vs NoSQL
column22:
h3. Summary

This issue involves creating a comparison report between Firebase and Supabase for a legal document summarization project. The report evaluates the best database architecture and backend platform.

h3. Context

The report is intended for project stakeholders and is authored by the Lead Software Engineer. It addresses the selection of a primary database and BaaS provider, focusing on the trade-offs between relational and NoSQL systems.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* Evaluate relational (PostgreSQL) and NoSQL (MongoDB/Firestore) systems.
* Justifies a selection between relational or non relational db, comparing the benefits and limitations of each
* Compare Supabase and Firebase as BaaS providers. Note that firebase has higher costs when scaled than supabase. Also note that supabase is open source and can be self hosted.
* Analyze data model fit, query patterns, and full-text search capabilities.
* Provide a comparison table of database capabilities.
* Include authentication integration details and migration costs.
* Present cost projections for different user scales.
* Justify the recommendation for Supabase (PostgreSQL) over Firebase.
* Outline next steps for implementation.

h3. Other information

* The report concludes that a relational approach powered by Supabase (PostgreSQL) is superior for scalability, cost predictability, and structural integrity.
* Next steps include:
*# Finalizing the migration of the {{DocumentProcessingPipeline}} to the Supabase {{documents}} table.
*# Configuring RLS policies for {{entities}} and {{summaries}} tables.
*# Saving the report to {{docs/database-comparison-report.md}}.(

column1: `analyze_document` lost `pre_extracted_entities` parameter

h3. Impact

The system should pass {{pre_extracted_entities=entities}} to the LLM summariser. This allows the LLM to focus on summarization without re-discovering entities.

h3. Steps to reproduce

* Review the code in {{backend/src/controllers/document.py}}.
* Check the implementation of the {{analyze_document}} method.
* Observe that {{pre_extracted_entities}} is not being passed to the LLM summariser.

N/A

column1: Add Basic Error Handling
column22:
h2. Description

The backend lacks centralised error handling. Exceptions can bubble up as unhandled 500 errors, and error messages may expose internal details. This task adds:

1. Global Exception Handlers:

  • Register exception handlers for RequestValidationError, HTTPException, and unhandled Exception.

  • Never expose stack traces or internal paths in production responses.

2. Structured Error Responses:

  • All errors return: {"success": false, "error": {"code": "ERROR_CODE", "message": "Human-readable message", "details": {...}}}

3. Logging:

  • Add structured logging with JSON formatting.

  • Log all errors with traceback at ERROR level.

  • Log all requests at INFO level with method, path, status code, and duration.

4. Graceful Degradation:

  • If LLM backend is unavailable, return a partial result with extracted text and entities but a note that summarisation is unavailable.

  • If a file cannot be parsed, return a clear error indicating which file and why.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

⬜ Global exception handlers are registered and catch all unhandled exceptions.

⬜ Error responses never expose stack traces or internal paths.

⬜ All errors follow the structured {"success": false, "error": {...}} format.

⬜ Request logging is implemented with method, path, status code, and duration.

⬜ LLM summarisation failure returns partial results instead of a 500 error.

⬜ File parsing failures return clear, user-friendly error messages.

⬜ Logs are written to both stdout (for Docker) and a rotating file handler.

column1: Test API Using Python Scripts
column22:
h2. Description

Create Python test scripts to validate all API endpoints programmatically. These scripts should:

1. Test Scripts:

  • scripts/test_api_upload.py — Test file upload with valid/invalid files.

  • scripts/test_api_process.py — Test the process endpoint, verify async job creation.

  • scripts/test_api_result.py — Test the result retrieval, verify full pipeline output.

  • scripts/test_api_error_handling.py — Test error scenarios.

  • scripts/test_api_full_flow.py — End-to-end test: upload → process → poll → verify result.

2. Test Coverage:

  • Happy path: valid file upload, successful processing, correct result format.

  • Error paths: invalid file type, oversized file, missing file, non-existent document_id.

  • Edge cases: empty files, very large files, files with unusual characters in names.

3. Reporting:

  • Scripts should output pass/fail for each test case.

  • Optional: generate a simple HTML or JSON report.

h2. Acceptance Criteria

⬜ All test scripts run successfully against a running backend instance.

⬜ Happy path tests pass: upload valid PDF/DOCX/TXT → process → get result with text + entities + summary.

⬜ Error path tests return appropriate HTTP status codes and error messages.

⬜ Edge case tests handle empty files, oversized files gracefully.

⬜ A README.md in scripts/ documents how to run the tests.

⬜ Test scripts can be run with a single command: python scripts/test_api_full_flow.py.

⬜ Test scripts accept a --base-url argument to target different environments.
